claims.statement: Erdős and Rényi 1960 On the Evolution of Random Graphs studies successively added uniformly sampled edges
1959 On Random Graphs I already studies full connectedness threshold m=(n/2)log n
1960 paper identifies thresholds and studies component evolution m~cn including emergence of giant component
For finite undirected graphs mean degree 2m/n; m=n/2 corresponds average degree 1
Fixed average degree c<1 sparse ER graph has largest component order logarithmic in n
Fixed c>1 sparse ER graph has a unique giant component of asymptotically linear size
At critical window c=1 largest component has order n^(2/3); not a fixed single-edge event
For c>1 giant fraction solves s=1-exp(-cs); at c=1.2 s roughly 0.31 and c=2 roughly 0.797
Expected number of isolated nodes n(1-p)^(n-1) approximately n e^(-c) for p approximately c/n
Full connectivity occurs on scale c~log n, m~n log n/2, later than giant component threshold
Adding one edge may merge two components but does not necessarily make full graph connected nor create a giant in one step
